sources.title: MIVUBI Entity Spawn Despawn and Population Integrity Policy v1

facts.subject: entity creation path
facts.statement: Classify every gameplay entity creation path as NATURAL_RULE, SCRIPT_SPAWN, COMMAND_SUMMON, STRUCTURE_RESTORE, PARENT_SPAWN_ENTITY, SPAWN_ON_DEATH, or RECOVERY_RESTORE so analyzer can reason about duplicates and ownership across heterogeneous spawn sources.

facts.subject: scripted gameplay spawn
facts.statement: Critical scripted spawns should carry a spawn intent or generation token containing arenaGeneration, waveGeneration, spawnOperationId, expected entity type, and expected count; repeated callbacks must not create extra entities for the same logical intent.

facts.subject: spawn verification
facts.statement: After critical spawn, verify entity identity, location, arena ownership, entityGeneration, and registry membership before treating the spawn as committed. API or command success alone is not sufficient for wave/objective accounting.

facts.subject: entity disappearance
facts.statement: Classify disappearance evidence into DEAD_CONFIRMED, DESPAWN_CONFIRMED_OR_EXPECTED, UNLOADED, EXPLICIT_REMOVE, REPLACED, and UNKNOWN. Do not decrement kill objectives merely because an entity is no longer queryable.

facts.subject: critical arena entity
facts.statement: Entities required for arena progression should have an explicit persistence/despawn policy. If default despawn behavior can remove them, either disable/override that path where appropriate or design recovery and objective logic that tolerates expected despawn.

facts.subject: arena population isolation
facts.statement: If arena objectives depend on precise enemy counts, distinguish arena-owned scripted entities from unrelated natural mobs sharing the same type or population pool. Broad type selectors must not become authoritative enemy registries.

facts.subject: autonomous spawn components
facts.statement: Audit entity definitions for minecraft:spawn_entity and spawn_on_death when diagnosing unexplained population growth or replacement entities; these spawn paths can operate independently of arena script spawn functions.

facts.subject: natural spawn failure
facts.statement: When a natural/data-driven spawn fails, inspect population pool pressure and density limits before concluding that spawn conditions or identifiers are wrong.

facts.subject: wave population
facts.statement: Wave/objective counts should be derived from generation-scoped registered entities plus lifecycle evidence, not from ambient world counts or decrement-only counters.

facts.subject: arena reset population
facts.statement: Arena reset must reconcile all arena-owned population sources and products: live entities, children/replacements, projectiles where relevant, autonomous spawn components, pending spawn callbacks, and spawn-on-death chains before reuse.

facts.subject: mass spawning
facts.statement: Burst spawning, recovery spawning, and autonomous population growth must obey per-arena/global performance budgets; a logically correct wave system can still cause watchdog pressure if many entities are created or initialized in one tick.

facts.subject: replacement entity lineage
facts.statement: When death or entity components create replacement/child entities, track lineage from source entity and decide whether the replacement inherits objective membership, arenaGeneration, and scoring role; inheritance must not be implicit.
